en.headline: Customs seizes three live cats at Lok Ma Chau Spur Line
en.dek: A 56-year-old Mainland woman was arrested after three suspected illegally imported cats valued at about HK$30,000 were found in her rucksack at the control point.
body: Hong Kong Customs detected a suspected case of illegal animal import at the Lok Ma Chau Spur Line Control Point on Monday and seized three live cats with an estimated market value of about HK$30,000.

Officers intercepted a 56-year-old incoming Mainland female passenger at the Arrival Hall. Upon examination, three live cats were found in her rucksack and she was arrested. The case was handed over to the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department for follow-up investigation.

Customs reminded the public that importing animals into Hong Kong without a valid permit is an offence. Under the Rabies Regulation, anyone found guilty of illegally importing animals, carcasses or animal products is liable to a maximum fine of HK$50,000 and imprisonment for one year.

zh.headline: 海關落馬洲支線檢三隻懷疑非法進口活貓
zh.dek: 海關周一在落馬洲支線管制站截獲一名56歲內地女旅客，在其背囊檢獲三隻估計市值約3萬元的活貓，並將其拘捕。
body: 香港海關周一在落馬洲支線管制站偵破一宗懷疑非法進口動物案件，檢獲三隻活貓，估計市值約3萬元。
關員在抵港大堂截查一名56歲內地女旅客，在其背囊發現三隻活貓，隨即拘捕她。案件已交予漁農自然護理署跟進調查。
海關提醒市民，未經許可進口動物屬違法。根據《狂犬病規例》，非法進口動物、動物屍體或動物產品，最高可被罰款5萬元及監禁一年。
